questions.q: How does a secondary ledger connect to its primary ledger in the data model?
options: Through a PRIMARY_LEDGER_ID column on GL_LEDGERS pointing back to the primary
Secondary ledgers are not represented in GL_LEDGERS at all
Through the CODE_COMBINATION_ID column
Through a PARTY_ID column
questions.explain: GL_LEDGERS stores every ledger's definition, and a secondary ledger's row carries PRIMARY_LEDGER_ID referencing its associated primary ledger.

questions.q: What happens if a period is Permanently Closed and a correction is needed?
options: The ledger itself must be deleted and recreated
The permanently closed period can simply be reopened and edited
The correction must be posted to a different, open period — permanently closed cannot be undone
Nothing — permanently closed periods accept new journals automatically
questions.explain: Permanently Closed is irreversible; corrections go into a currently open period instead.

questions.q: Why does Oracle Fusion maintain GL_BALANCES rather than having every report sum GL_JE_LINES directly?
options: GL_JE_LINES doesn't actually store amounts
Pre-summarized balances by account, period, and currency are far faster for reporting than re-aggregating every journal line on demand
GL_BALANCES is only used for budgets, never actuals
Reports are legally required to avoid GL_JE_LINES
questions.explain: GL_BALANCES stores pre-summarized actual, budget, and encumbrance balances specifically so reports don't have to re-sum every journal line each time.

questions.q: What is the shared key that connects GL_JE_HEADERS/LINES, GL_PERIODS, and GL_BALANCES?
options: CUSTOMER_TRX_ID
VENDOR_ID
PARTY_ID
PERIOD_NAME
questions.explain: PERIOD_NAME ties a journal's posting period to the period's calendar definition and status, and to the balances summarized for that same period.

questions.q: What are the four defining attributes of a ledger, first introduced in lesson 2 and stored on GL_LEDGERS?
options: Batch, header, line, period
Party, account, site, site-use
Chart of accounts, calendar, currency, convention
Invoice, line, distribution, payment
questions.explain: The "four Cs" — chart of accounts, calendar, currency, and accounting convention — define each ledger stored in GL_LEDGERS.
